headline: Zcash surges 17% as privacy coins catch a bid; UBS and Jane Street hold $75M in Hyperliquid ETFs
summary: The day's standout move was Zcash, which jumped 17.4% to $1,187.27 as traders rotated into privacy-focused assets alongside a 2.58% gain in Monero. Solana and Dogecoin also outperformed, rising 3.8% and 4.35% respectively, while Bitcoin drifted up 0.45% to $79,980 and Ethereum gained 1.79%. The bigger institutional story: UBS and Jane Street have together accumulated $75 million in Hyperliquid ETF exposure, a sign that traditional finance is moving beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum when it comes to crypto products.

winners.name: Zcash
winners.catalyst: Zcash surged 17.40% to $1,187.27, driven by a broad rotation into privacy coins — Monero gained 2.58% on the same day. No single news event triggered the move; the pattern points to renewed demand for assets that offer transaction privacy as regulatory surveillance concerns persist.

losers.name: Bittensor
losers.catalyst: Bittensor slipped 0.42% — the day's weakest performer among tracked non-stablecoin assets, though the move was too small to point to any specific catalyst.

whyItMoved:
The clearest story today was in privacy coins. Zcash jumped 17.4% and Monero gained 2.58% — both moving together in a pattern that suggests capital rotating into assets designed to obscure transaction trails. No specific news event triggered the Zcash move, but the broader context is a persistent undercurrent of concern about blockchain surveillance and regulatory monitoring of on-chain activity. When that concern flares, privacy-focused assets tend to catch a bid simultaneously, which is what happened here.

Beyond privacy coins, the session had a broadly constructive tone. Solana rose 3.8%, Dogecoin gained 4.35%, and Hyperliquid climbed 3.5% — the last of those supported by a concrete institutional catalyst: UBS and Jane Street disclosed a combined $75 million in Hyperliquid ETF holdings, a meaningful signal that traditional finance firms are building exposure to on-chain derivatives infrastructure, not just Bitcoin and Ethereum.

Bitcoin itself was quiet, gaining just 0.45% to $79,980. With BTC dominance at 59.23% and the Fear & Greed index at 73 (Greed territory), the market's overall mood was positive but the day's energy was in smaller assets rather than the flagship. Ethereum added 1.79%, in line with the broader altcoin tone.
worthKnowing: A Bank of Korea study found that dollar-backed stablecoins can suppress local currency values, raising the prospect of tighter sovereign restrictions on stablecoin adoption in markets outside the US.
Tether-backed exchange Orionx is shutting down after an audit identified a $7 million gap in customer custody holdings, adding to scrutiny of crypto custodial practices.
Poland's legislature upheld a presidential veto on a crypto regulatory bill while the Zondacrypto exchange scandal continued to widen, leaving the country's regulatory framework unresolved.
